[under: About the Company] Crown Holdings, Inc. is a global leader in the design, manufacture, and sale of packaging products for consumer goods.
[under: About the Company] With operations in 39 countries employing over 23,000 people and net sales of over $11 billion, we are uniquely positioned to bring best practices in quality and manufacturing to our customers to drive their businesses locally and globally.
[under: About the Company] Sustaining a leadership position requires us to build a team of highly talented, dedicated, and driven individuals.
[under: About the Team] The Global Information Security Team’s mission is “protect Crown’s global information systems, data and employees from cyber-based security threats while ensuring the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information used by the Crown business units to produce world class sustainable packaging solutions to our customers”.
# Location
[under: Location] Yardley, PA (USA) or Wantage (UK).
[under: Location] This is an office-based position, and individuals are expected to be in the office daily.
[under: About the Position] The OT Security Technical Lead is responsible for designing, implementing, and continuously improving cybersecurity controls across Crown’s global manufacturing OT environments, including industrial control systems, factory automation systems, and other OT technologies as needed.
[under: About the Position] Partnering with the regional IT teams, manufacturing plant personnel and the rest of the Global Security Team, they will implement and maintain OT security solutions and ensure all OT related systems are securely configured to protect against current and emerging cyber threats and align with Crown security standards.
[under: Strategy and Architecture Design (30%)] - Identify, assess, and select global OT security related solutions and changes that improve Crown’s OT cybersecurity posture across its global operations.
[under: Stakeholder Collaboration and Consulting (30%)] - Work with regional IT teams, plant engineers and operators to ensure security controls are feasible, maintainable, and do not compromise production or safety.
[under: Requirements] Crown seeks an experienced and driven OT Security Technical Lead to drive improvement in Crown’s overall OT security by designing and engineering resilient, secure solutions and controls and coordinating their implementation across its global manufacturing environment.
[under: Technical Expertise] - Proficient in OT network architecture and security controls, including network segmentation, firewalls, industrial DMZs, secure remote access, and secure communications.
[under: Core Competencies] - Excellent communication skills; translates technical concepts for diverse audiences and influences technical stakeholders through evidence-based recommendations.
[under: Core Competencies] - Personable and relationship-focused; builds trusted, productive working relationships across teams, stakeholders, countries, and cultures to enable effective collaboration and shared outcomes.

text:
company: CoreWeave Europe
title: Solution Specialist, Infrastructure
options: London, UK [undeclared]
description:
> Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability.
[under: What You'll Do] The AI infrastructure market is moving faster than any playbook can keep up with, and the companies building at its frontier, from early-stage European startups to the world's largest enterprises with operations across EMEA, need a commercial partner who understands their infrastructure requirements as instinctively as they do.
[under: What You'll Do] As a Principal Solution Specialist for Infrastructure, EMEA, you sit at the center of how CoreWeave structures, negotiates, and closes its most complex infrastructure deals across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, while operating as a fully integrated member of CoreWeave's global infrastructure deal team.
[under: What You'll Do] This is not a single-product or single-vertical role: it requires deep fluency in how AI companies across EMEA think about and consume infrastructure, and it turns that fluency into the commercial mechanics, deal frameworks, and cross-functional alignment that make large-scale infrastructure commitments possible in one of the world's most strategically important AI markets.
[under: About the role] As a Principal Solution Specialist for Infrastructure, EMEA, you design the frameworks that govern how CoreWeave structures large infrastructure commitments for EMEA customers, negotiate the commercial terms that create durable value for both sides, and build the playbooks and processes the EMEA field team relies on to win.
[under: About the role] But this role goes beyond deal mechanics: you will develop an instinctive understanding of what AI companies in EMEA need to build across every layer of the infrastructure stack, and across every stage of company maturity from early-stage startup to hyperscale enterprise.
[under: About the role] In a market changing as fast as AI infrastructure, the intelligence you gather from EMEA customer conversations feeds directly into CoreWeave's global product, engineering, capacity planning, finance, and marketing teams.
[under: About the role] This role sits at the intersection of sales, operations, enablement, and deal desk, and the regional insight it generates shapes how CoreWeave builds and goes to market across EMEA.
[under: In this role, you will] - Own the end-to-end commercial and operational lifecycle of CoreWeave's most complex infrastructure deals across EMEA, from initial deal architecture through term negotiation, contract execution, and account expansion.
[under: In this role, you will] - Structure and close large-scale infrastructure commitments across EMEA, from long-term compute and networking agreements to integrated AI platform deals, in close coordination with sales, legal, finance, and product teams across CoreWeave.
[under: In this role, you will] - Design deal frameworks, pricing models, and term structures suited to EMEA enterprise and sovereign AI procurement dynamics, reflecting what AI companies need to build at scale while meeting data residency, regulatory compliance, and cost predictability requirements.
[under: In this role, you will] - Own the deal desk function for EMEA infrastructure commitments, providing real-time deal guidance, commercial structuring support, and pricing alignment to the EMEA field team and to global opportunities with EMEA decision-making centers.
[under: In this role, you will] - Enable the EMEA sales and solutions architecture organizations with infrastructure deal playbooks, term negotiation frameworks, TCO models, and region-specific competitive positioning materials that accelerate large infrastructure closings.
[under: In this role, you will] - Engage directly with EMEA customer procurement, legal, and executive leadership, across enterprise technology companies, financial institutions, and sovereign AI programs, as CoreWeave's primary commercial voice in complex, multi-stakeholder infrastructure negotiations.
[under: In this role, you will] - Partner with global product specialists across Core Services, AI Runtime, AI Developer Services, and Data Services to build integrated deal proposals that reflect the full value of CoreWeave's infrastructure platform for EMEA customers.
[under: In this role, you will] - Serve as the EMEA field's primary intelligence source on how AI companies across European and Middle Eastern industries and company stages think about and consume infrastructure, translating regional customer conversations into direct input for CoreWeave's global product, engineering, capacity planning, finance, and marketing teams.
[under: In this role, you will] - Drive operational consistency between EMEA and global deal processes, including deal review cadences, cross-regional escalation paths, and post-signature execution handoffs, to ensure CoreWeave operates as a cohesive global commercial organization.
[under: Who You Are] - 10+ years of experience in enterprise infrastructure sales, deal structuring, or commercial operations at a cloud provider, hyperscaler, data center operator, or large-scale technology vendor in EMEA markets, with a track record of closing large, complex deals.
[under: Who You Are] - 5+ years owning or shaping the commercial structure of large infrastructure commitments in EMEA, including cloud compute agreements, GPU infrastructure contracts, data center agreements, or equivalent, spanning term negotiation, pricing strategy, and contract execution in a customer-facing capacity.
[under: Who You Are] - Deep understanding of how AI companies across EMEA, from startups building their first production systems to enterprises scaling global AI deployments, evaluate, procure, and operationalize infrastructure, including the technical, financial, regulatory, and organizational dynamics that drive those decisions across key EMEA markets.
[under: Who You Are] - Fluency across CoreWeave's infrastructure portfolio, GPU compute, high-performance networking, storage, and Kubernetes platform, and strong working knowledge of how these components combine into integrated infrastructure commitments for AI customers in EMEA.
[under: Who You Are] - Familiarity with EMEA regulatory considerations that shape AI infrastructure procurement, including GDPR, EU AI Act requirements, data residency obligations, and sovereign AI program dynamics, and how these translate into deal structure and contract terms.
[under: Who You Are] - Track record of engaging at the executive level with EMEA customers, C-suite, VP-level procurement, and legal leadership, across complex, multi-stakeholder commercial negotiations at major enterprises, financial institutions, and public sector organizations.
[under: Who You Are] - Commercial fluency across deal structures: long-term commitment economics, ramp schedules, SLA frameworks, and the financial tradeoffs that shape large infrastructure agreements for AI companies in EMEA enterprise contexts.
[under: Preferred] - Prior experience in a deal desk, commercial operations, or strategic deals function at a cloud provider or hyperscaler operating in EMEA (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Oracle Cloud, or equivalent).
[under: Preferred] - Background in AI infrastructure procurement or sales in EMEA, with direct experience structuring GPU infrastructure agreements, HPC contracts, or large-scale cloud commitments for AI/ML workloads with European or Middle Eastern customers.
[under: Preferred] - Experience navigating EMEA-specific commercial and legal frameworks, including VAT structures, cross-border contract considerations, and sovereign procurement requirements, in the context of large technology infrastructure deals.
[under: Preferred] - Advanced degree in Business, Finance, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent experience with a demonstrated ability to operate at the intersection of commercial strategy, technical infrastructure, and EMEA market dynamics.
[under: Wondering if you're a good fit?] - You love sitting at the center of complex deals: you are energized by multi-workstream negotiations where legal, finance, product, and engineering are all in the room and something significant has to close, and you bring EMEA-specific commercial judgment to every stage.
[under: Wondering if you're a good fit?] - You love acting as the bridge: between the EMEA field team's customer commitments and the global commercial, operational, and financial machinery that makes those commitments real, and you hold both sides accountable.
[under: Wondering if you're a good fit?] - You are an expert at navigating "The Room": you have a proven ability to manage complex, multi-stakeholder commercial negotiations across EMEA enterprise, financial, and public sector organizations, without losing momentum, clarity, or trust.
